claims.claim: Runtime provides provider interfaces for implementing custom LLM providers
Quick start compiles: stage.NewPipelineBuilder().Chain(stage.NewProviderStage(provider, nil, nil, &stage.ProviderConfig{MaxTokens, Temperature})).Build()
openai.NewProvider(id, model, baseURL, providers.ProviderDefaults{Temperature, MaxTokens}, includeRawOutput)
types.Message{Role: "user"}.AddTextPart; stage.NewMessageElement(&msg); pipeline.Execute(ctx, input) returns (output, err); elem.Text is *string
Stage interface has Name, Type, Process(ctx, input, output)
Stage types Transform, Accumulate, Generate, Sink with patterns 1:1/1:N, N:1, 0:N, N:0
tools Executor interface: Execute(ctx, descriptor, args) and Name()
Architecture diagram: SDK -> Pipeline -> Stages -> Providers/Tools/Hooks; Providers -> OpenAI, Anthropic; Tools -> MCP
Text mode flow: StateStoreLoad -> PromptAssembly -> Provider -> StateStoreSave
VAD mode flow: AudioTurn -> STT -> Provider -> TTS
StreamElement struct fields (Text, Audio, Video, Image, Message, ToolCall, Part, MediaData, Sequence, Timestamp, Source, Priority, Meta, EndOfStream, EndOfTurn, Interrupt, Error)
PredictionResponse has Content, Parts, CostInfo, Latency, ToolCalls
Priority values Low, Normal, High, Critical
Runtime has backpressure support, minimal allocations, connection pooling
All linked docs pages exist; Storage API page covers state storage
Questions link goes to GitHub Discussions
OpenAI provider reads its API key from OPENAI_API_KEY or OPENAI_TOKEN
